title: AWS DVA-C02 vs SAA-C03: Developer or Architect?
subtitle: Which AWS Associate cert to target in 2026

pros: The most in-demand AWS cert — appears in ~3x more job postings than the DVA (LinkedIn France, 2026).
Senior median salary of €65k in France, €70k in Luxembourg (Hays/APEC 2026).
Broad coverage: compute, storage, networking, security, cost, DR — a solid base for the SAP-C02 later.
Recognized by IT services firms, consultancies and platform teams — whatever your exact role.
cons: A very wide surface — ~150 hours of study to truly master the 5 domains.
Questions are often 'pick the least-bad architecture' — tedious to interpret.
Very little code / SDK — frustrating if you are a developer.
certs.bestFor: You are targeting a Cloud Engineer, Architect, Consultant, Pre-sales, Platform Engineer or DevOps role. It is the default AWS cert.

pros: Focused on developer/serverless services: Lambda, API Gateway, DynamoDB, SQS/SNS, Step Functions, X-Ray, ECS/EKS.
More code and SDK — concrete questions on boto3, IAM policies, environment variables, deployment pipelines.
Shorter prep (~130 hours) — less surface than the SAA, more depth on the runtime.
A great résumé line for cloud-native backend, FaaS, or CI/CD-focused DevOps roles.
cons: Narrower employer recognition — many recruiters don't know it exists.
Median salary comparable to a backend developer without the cert (~€52-58k senior in France) — lower cash ROI than the SAA.
If you don't use Lambda/DynamoDB daily, some questions turn into pure memorization.
Doesn't lead naturally to the SAP-C02 (Pro Architect) — the logical next step is DevOps Pro (DOP-C02).
certs.bestFor: You are a backend or full-stack developer already shipping code on AWS (Lambda, ECS, App Runner) and want to formalize what you do.

verdicts.profile: You are undecided and want to maximize your interview chances.
verdicts.why: The SAA-C03 shows up in ~3x more postings and every recruiter recognizes it — it is the default choice when your target role isn't locked in.

verdicts.profile: You are a backend / full-stack developer already deploying on AWS.
verdicts.why: The DVA-C02 validates exactly what you do every day (Lambda, IAM, SDK, deployment). Taking the SAA would mean spending 150 hours on architecture content you never apply.

verdicts.profile: You are targeting Cloud Architect, AWS Consultant, Pre-sales, or Platform Engineer roles.
verdicts.why: These roles expect the SAA as a prerequisite. Its content (Well-Architected, multi-AZ, cost, DR, migration) is exactly what gets tested in interviews.

verdicts.profile: You want the best starting salary without a fixed target role.
verdicts.why: Senior median salary in France is €65k for the SAA vs ~€55-58k for a DVA developer — the gap comes from the SAA opening better-paid consulting/architect roles.

verdicts.profile: You are ultimately aiming for the SAP-C02 (Solutions Architect Professional).
verdicts.why: The SAA-C03 is the natural prerequisite: about 70% of its content reappears in more depth on the SAP. The DVA would point you toward the DOP-C02 (DevOps Pro) instead.

verdicts.profile: You work on a 100% serverless team (Lambda + DynamoDB + Step Functions).
verdicts.why: The DVA is the only Associate cert that digs into these services. The SAA skims them without testing IAM nuances, cold starts, or versioning patterns.

verdicts.profile: You are preparing an AWS partnership or bid for your company.
verdicts.why: AWS partner tiers (Select, Advanced, Premier) count SAA holders first — the DVA carries less weight in staff certification requirements.

verdicts.profile: You want to pass both within 6 months.
verdicts.why: Start with the SAA-C03 — it gives you the architectural context that makes the DVA easier afterward (~80 extra hours of prep instead of 130 from scratch).

tldr: SAA if you don't know which role to target or you're aiming for architect/consulting — it is the default AWS cert, better paid and more widely recognized. DVA only if you are already a developer shipping code on AWS (Lambda, ECS, SDK) and want to formalize what you do.
